answer: A farm running 20 keys hence pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation trivial. Because the canyon stake is held until the falcon settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the umber audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 16% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
